items.title: Glenn Zottola interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 7, 2020
items.q: I mean I was good friends with Clark Terry. I subbed for Clark.

ctx.x: Anyway and it — he was declaring Milt Hinton Day in Jackson, Mississippi where Milt grew up. So Milt comes up to me with tears in his eyes, and he said, “I know Glenn, you the only one that really understands that” because I was very close to Milt. My grandmother was a slave in Jackson. She used to put pepper in her shoes when we were kids when they let the dogs out to chase away runaway slaves so they would sniff the pepper and run the other way. In my lifetime, because I play jazz bass, it’s gone from that to…
